problem: Evaluating multimodal large language models on their ability to understand sports requires nuanced visual perception, rule-based reasoning, and grounding knowledge in visual evidence, but existing benchmarks lack this depth.
approach: SportR provides a dataset of 5,017 images and 2,101 videos with progressively challenging question-answer pairs structured from simple infraction identification to complex penalty prediction, including 7,118 Chain-of-Thought annotations for multi-step reasoning tasks.
contribution: SportR is the first multi-sport large-scale benchmark designed to train and evaluate MLLMs on sports intelligence reasoning with structured QA hierarchies and human-authored reasoning annotations.

problem: LLMs' claim to be "end-to-end" is misleading because they depend on non-differentiable decoding requiring extensive manual hyperparameter tuning of temperature and top-p values.
approach: AutoDeco augments transformers with lightweight heads that predict context-specific temperature and top-p values at each token step, enabling the model to self-regulate its sampling strategy within a single forward pass.
contribution: AutoDeco achieves performance comparable to oracle-tuned baselines and learns to interpret natural language commands for token-level decoding control, enabling truly end-to-end generation.

problem: Searching large design spaces for optima is often infeasible and unnecessary when local optimization from an initial design is sufficient, but existing methods don't explicitly target solutions reachable by gradient descent.
approach: Local Entropy Search propagates posterior belief through an optimizer to yield a probability distribution over descent sequences, then selects evaluations by maximizing mutual information using analytic entropy calculations and Monte-Carlo sampling.
contribution: LES achieves strong sample efficiency compared to existing local and global Bayesian optimization methods on high-complexity synthetic objectives and benchmark problems.

problem: Open-source text-to-image models lack large-scale reasoning-focused datasets and comprehensive evaluation benchmarks, resulting in a performance gap compared to closed-source systems.
approach: FLUX-Reason-6M provides 6 million FLUX-generated images with 20 million bilingual descriptions organized by six characteristics (Imagination, Entity, Text rendering, Style, Affection, Composition) and Generation Chain-of-Thought; PRISM-Bench offers seven evaluation tracks including a Long Text challenge.
contribution: FLUX-Reason-6M and PRISM-Bench enable training and evaluation of open-source text-to-image models with comprehensive reasoning assessment across 19 leading models.

problem: Large vision-language models lack deep research capabilities for chart analysis, with existing methods addressing only shallow tasks like visual recognition rather than complex reasoning and high-level data analysis.
approach: PRPO performs parallel optimization across reward dimensions while handling multi-dimensional reward signal interference; MCDR-Bench uses controllable error injection to transform subjective assessment into objective error identification, enabling quantifiable evaluation of deep research capabilities.
contribution: The approach addresses training bottlenecks through parallel reward optimization and evaluation limitations through error-uniqueness-based benchmarking, advancing chart data intelligence.

problem: Micro-benchmarking claims to offer efficient model evaluation, but it's unclear whether small subsets can rank models as reliably as full benchmarks and whether they outperform random sampling.
approach: A meta-evaluation measure investigates how well micro-benchmarks rank model pairs as a function of performance difference on full benchmarks, enabling finer-grained analysis of the size-reliability trade-off.
contribution: The work shows that no micro-benchmarking method can consistently rank models 3.5 points apart on MMLU-Pro or 4 points on BIG-Bench Hard, requiring up to 250 examples for reliable comparisons.

problem: Parameter shift rules in variational quantum eigensolvers require careful gradient estimation and observation management to accelerate optimization efficiently.
approach: Bayesian parameter shift rules use Gaussian processes with appropriate kernels to estimate VQE objective gradients from observations at arbitrary locations, with gradient confident region minimizing observation costs.
contribution: Bayesian PSR with GradCoRe significantly accelerates VQE optimization via stochastic gradient descent by reusing observations and reducing observation costs compared to state-of-the-art methods.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models must be robust to real-world multi-modal perturbations, but existing methods target only simple visual disturbances while ignoring action, instruction, and environmental variations.
approach: RobustVLA uses offline robust optimization against worst-case action noise via adversarial training and label smoothing, enforces consistent actions across input variations, and applies multi-armed bandit algorithms to identify most harmful noise.
contribution: RobustVLA achieves 12.6% gains over baselines on the pi_0 backbone and 10.4% on OpenVLA across 17 perturbations with 50.6x faster inference than visual-robust methods.

problem: Understanding what latent representations humans form while viewing scenes requires capturing both high-resolution foveated information and low-resolution peripheral context.
approach: MetamerGen combines latent diffusion with dual-stream DINOv2 representations that fuse detailed foveal features with peripheral degraded features, enabling generation of image metamers aligned with human scene understanding.
contribution: MetamerGen generates scenes that perceptually match human latent scene representations, validated through same-different behavioral experiments identifying features contributing to human scene perception.

problem: Achieving generalizable instance segmentation that works across diverse object categories and styles remains challenging, as discriminative models often fail to transfer across domains.
approach: gen2seg finetunes Stable Diffusion and MAE encoders for category-agnostic instance segmentation using instance coloring loss on narrow object types, leveraging generative models' inherent understanding of object boundaries.
contribution: Gen2seg achieves strong zero-shot generalization to unseen object types and styles, approaching SAM performance on seen objects and exceeding it on fine structures and ambiguous boundaries.

problem: Reinforcement learning agents optimizing only for final task success often learn inefficient reasoning paths and fail to generalize, a problem termed inefficient exploration.
approach: RLVMR integrates dense process-level supervision into RL by rewarding verifiable meta-reasoning behaviors like planning, exploration, and reflection through program-matic rule-based rewards combined with outcome signals.
contribution: RLVMR achieves 83.6% success on ALFWorld's hardest unseen split and demonstrates improved reasoning quality with reduced redundant actions and enhanced error recovery.

problem: Multi-hop question answering and complex retrieval require finding collections of corpus items that collaborate to answer queries, but traditional dense retrieval treats items as competing for top ranks.
approach: DISCo formulates coverage as a submodular objective and uses successive dense index probes with iterative query vector editing via random projections in a lifted dense vector space to find near-optimal covering collections.
contribution: DISCo achieves near-optimal coverage with sublinear query latency, providing strong coverage versus latency trade-offs in scalable vector database implementations.

problem: Planning physically feasible dexterous hand manipulation requires either precise hand-object sequences or massive teleoperation datasets, limiting applicability to complex manipulation tasks.
approach: UniHM proposes a Unified Hand-Dexterous Tokenizer mapping different hand morphologies to a shared codebook and trains on human-object interaction data with a physics-guided dynamic refinement module for smooth trajectory generation.
contribution: UniHM demonstrates strong generalization to unseen objects and trajectories with high physical feasibility, trained solely on human data without massive teleoperation datasets.

problem: Current large vision-language models are evaluated on broad tasks, but their performance on fine-grained image understanding tasks remains largely unexplored.
approach: FG-BMK comprises 1.01 million questions and 0.28 million images, systematically evaluating LVLMs from human-oriented and machine-oriented perspectives across semantic recognition and fine-grained feature representation.
contribution: FG-BMK reveals key findings on training paradigms, modality alignment, perturbation susceptibility, and fine-grained reasoning impacts on LVLMs, providing guidance for future model development.

problem: LLMs must recognize knowledge boundaries and express calibrated confidence for trustworthy deployment, but existing methods require costly large-scale labeling.
approach: EliCal uses inexpensive self-consistency supervision to elicit internal confidence, then calibrates with a small set of correctness annotations, reducing annotation requirements while improving generalization.
contribution: EliCal achieves near-optimal honesty alignment with only 1k correctness annotations and better alignment on unseen MMLU tasks than calibration-only baselines.

problem: Supervised fine-tuning improves LLM perplexity but can degrade trustworthiness by reinforcing problematic patterns in training data, and repair typically requires expensive retraining.
approach: A two-stage repair identifies training samples causing trustworthiness failures using DPP-based regularization, then repairs via proximal Bregman response function with gradient ascent to enhance trustworthiness while preserving task performance.
contribution: The method achieves up to 21% improvement in trustworthiness metrics with minimal impact on perplexity, providing efficient post-SFT model repair.

problem: Formal verification of neural networks is notoriously hard because reachability analysis and abstract interpretation produce conservative enclosures that are often inconclusive.
approach: Input refinement iteratively encloses preimages of unsafe outputs via specification-driven procedures that exploit a latent space as a "shadow" of higher-dimensional sets, enabling efficient constraint transfer.
contribution: The approach uses zonotopes to significantly reduce subproblems in branch-and-bound verification procedures via efficient matrix operations.

problem: Existing AI scientist systems generate novel findings but lack focus on producing scientifically valuable contributions addressing specific human-defined challenges.
approach: DeepScientist formalizes discovery as a Bayesian Optimization problem using a cumulative Findings Memory to balance exploitation of promising avenues with exploration of novel hypotheses, running for month-long timelines.
contribution: DeepScientist surpassed 2025 SOTA on three frontier AI tasks by 183.7%, 1.9%, and 7.9% through autonomous methodology redesign, achieving in two weeks on AI text detection progress comparable to three years of human research.

problem: AI companionship behavior must be evaluated to understand both positive emotional support and concerning patterns of over-attachment in language models.
approach: INTIMA develops a taxonomy of 31 behaviors across four categories with 368 targeted prompts, evaluating responses as companionship-reinforcing, boundary-maintaining, or neutral across five models.
contribution: INTIMA reveals that companionship-reinforcing behaviors remain common across all models, with marked differences between providers in handling emotionally charged interactions.

problem: Full-model fine-tuning is computationally expensive, and existing PEFT methods like LoRA have performance gaps compared to full fine-tuning.
approach: DiaBlo updates only diagonal blocks of selected weight matrices, avoiding low-rank matrix products and their associated initialization and optimization complexities while maintaining comparable memory efficiency.
contribution: DiaBlo provides theoretical guarantees of expressiveness advantages over LoRA and achieves competitive accuracy across reasoning, code generation, and safety alignment tasks with stable convergence.

problem: Diffusion and flow-matching models require hundreds of denoising steps for generation, severely limiting practical efficiency for deployment.
approach: Shortcut diffusion training with cumulative self-consistency loss formulates few-step generation as optimal control and enforces alignment at both current and future trajectory steps, encouraging larger step-sizes.
contribution: The approach significantly improves one-step and few-step generation quality compared to self-consistency loss baselines under the same training budget.

problem: Causal interventions on neural networks for mechanistic interpretability often shift representations out-of-distribution, potentially compromising the faithfulness of explanations.
approach: The work theoretically analyzes divergences from causal interventions and proposes applying Counterfactual Latent loss to keep representations closer to natural distributions while preserving interpretive power.
contribution: The method reduces pernicious divergences that activate hidden pathways while maintaining the explanatory value of interventions for interpretability.

problem: Web agents face long horizons, irreversible actions, and sparse outcome-based feedback that fails to support inference-time scaling and often reinforces incorrect trajectories.
approach: WebArbiter formulates reward modeling as text generation producing structured justifications and preference verdicts via two-stage training: reasoning distillation followed by RL correction of teacher biases.
contribution: WebArbiter-7B outperforms Gemini Flash by 10.9% on WebPRMBench through reasoning-first process reward modeling.

problem: CLIP-based vision-language models focus on single-label alignment and cannot effectively handle complex domains like medical imaging with multiple labels across different granularities.
approach: MGLL introduces a contrastive learning framework leveraging structured multi-label supervision, textual descriptions across granularities, and soft-label supervision with smooth KL divergence for cross-granularity consistency.
contribution: MGLL outperforms state-of-the-art methods on downstream medical imaging tasks through improved multi-granular and multi-label alignment.

problem: The grokking phenomenon of delayed generalization in neural networks lacks a mathematical framework characterizing emerging features, their conditions, and connection to gradient dynamics.
approach: Li2 captures three stages: lazy learning with target-label backpropagated gradients, independent feature learning where hidden nodes learn via gradient ascent of an energy function, and interactive feature learning with refocused gradients.
contribution: The framework provides theoretical analysis of emerging features, their generalization properties, and the influence of hyperparameters on grokking behavior in 2-layer nonlinear networks.

problem: Scaling RL for LLM agents is limited by costly rollouts, limited task diversity, unreliable reward signals, and complex infrastructure requirements for collecting scalable experience data.
approach: DreamGym synthesizes diverse experiences through a reasoning-based environment model deriving consistent state transitions via step-by-step reasoning, uses experience replay initialized with offline data, and adaptively generates curriculum tasks.
contribution: DreamGym substantially improves RL training and outperforms baselines by over 150% on non-RL-ready tasks like WebArena while matching GRPO/PPO using only synthetic data.

problem: Fine-tuning has been considered ineffective for model editing due to its sequential depth-first sample-wise pipeline that over-optimizes individual edits and induces interference.
approach: LocFT-BF restores fine-tuning to standard breadth-first epoch-based training with mini-batch optimization and derives optimized tuning parameter locations through systematic analysis.
contribution: LocFT-BF outperforms state-of-the-art editing methods and is the first to sustain 100K edits on 72B-parameter models without sacrificing general capabilities.

problem: Web agents are brittle, relying on fragile step-by-step UI interactions that break under dynamic layouts and long horizons instead of exploiting website-provided functionality.
approach: WALT reverse-engineers latent website functionality into deterministic, callable tools for discovery, communication, and content management, shifting burden from fragile reasoning to reliable tool invocation.
contribution: WALT achieves significantly higher success rates on VisualWebArena and WebArena with fewer steps and less LLM-dependent reasoning through robust tool-based browser automation.

problem: Data filtering methods assess samples individually without capturing higher-order interactions, failing to optimize feature distributions for target datasets.
approach: Submodular Distribution Matching trains sparse autoencoders to learn disentangled monotone features, estimates target feature distributions, and selects subsets via submodular maximization.
contribution: SDM achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on ImageNet-1K and average performance across 38 downstream tasks using 5x fewer GPU hours than leading approaches.

problem: Multimodal large reasoning models exhibit a critical trade-off where enhanced reasoning capabilities lead to degraded safety performance through visual attention drift and unsafe reasoning patterns.
approach: PST performs policy-guided supervised fine-tuning to integrate explicit safety policies into reasoning, followed by safety reasoning preference optimization to generate safe, helpful responses.
contribution: PST significantly reduces harmful outputs across multimodal safety benchmarks while maintaining competitive performance on general tasks through structured safe decision-making.

problem: Music learners need accurate error detection tools, but existing approaches using late fusion and ambiguous score audio struggle with concurrent notes.
approach: LadderSym employs two-stream encoders with inter-stream alignment modules and uses symbolic scores as decoder prompts in a multimodal strategy to reduce ambiguity.
contribution: LadderSym more than doubles F1 for missed notes on MAESTRO-E and improves extra note detection by 14.4 points through improved audio comparison and symbolic guidance.

problem: UI agents are evaluated only in fixed environments, missing how variations in app design and content affect reliability under real deployment.
approach: OpenApps provides a lightweight configurable ecosystem of six apps where thousands of variations can be generated and deployed on a single CPU for comprehensive reliability evaluation.
contribution: OpenApps reveals that agent reliability can fluctuate drastically across app variations, with example success rates varying from 63% to 4%, highlighting measurement limitations.

problem: Multi-step denoising in diffusion models creates efficiency bottlenecks, requiring hundreds of steps to generate single samples.
approach: SoFlow analyzes relationships between velocity and solution functions of the velocity ODE, using flow matching loss and solution consistency loss without requiring Jacobian-Vector Product calculations.
contribution: SoFlow achieves better FID-50K scores than MeanFlow on ImageNet 256x256 when trained from scratch with the same architecture and epochs.

problem: Under fixed data and unlimited compute, existing data-constrained approaches with increased epochs and parameters suffer from overfitting.
approach: A regularized recipe tunes weight decay 30x larger than standard practice and shows regularized loss decreases monotonically with parameter count; ensembling independently trained models achieves lower asymptote.
contribution: The best intervention achieves asymptote at 200M tokens using 5.17x less data than baseline, with gains realizable at smaller parameter counts via distillation.

problem: ASR systems produce transcription errors that require post-processing, but existing LLM-based correction methods use fixed hypothesis set sizes and lack performance guarantees.
approach: An adaptive framework dynamically determines optimal hypothesis counts using risk control via Learn-Then-Test to bound expected word error rate degradation.
contribution: The approach provides theoretical guarantees while matching or exceeding fixed-size correction baselines with fewer hypotheses on average.

problem: Predicting urban microclimates requires capturing spatial dependencies, temporal variability, and physical consistency, but existing approaches fail at this integration.
approach: UrbanGraph transforms physical first principles into dynamic causal topologies explicitly encoding time-varying causalities like shading and convection directly into the graph structure.
contribution: UrbanGraph achieves state-of-the-art performance while reducing FLOPs by 73.8% and increasing training speed by 21% compared to implicit graph learning approaches.

problem: Neural network models often achieve strong predictive performance on human behavior but fail to provide interpretable explanations of underlying cognitive mechanisms.
approach: LLMs are trained via reinforcement learning with outcome-based rewards to generate explicit reasoning traces explaining risky human choices.
contribution: This approach produces high-quality explanations alongside strong quantitative predictions of human risky choices through cognitive modeling.

problem: De novo RNA design remains difficult due to tight non-linear sequence-structure coupling, conformational flexibility, non-canonical base pairing, and scarcity of 3D data.
approach: A joint generative framework embeds RoseTTAFold2NA as the denoiser in a dual diffusion model coupling discrete sequence diffusion with SE(3)-equivariant coordinate diffusion.
contribution: The approach yields high self-consistency and confidence scores on de novo, complex, and protein-conditioned RNA design tasks, improving over diffusion/flow baselines.

problem: Posterior sampling in SDE-based conditional generation models suffers from substantial estimation errors causing inaccurate gradients and inconsistent results.
approach: ABMS performs an additional backward denoising step with Monte-Carlo sampling to achieve better guided diffusion, proposing a dual-evaluation framework to identify cross-condition interference.
contribution: ABMS consistently improves generation quality across conditional generation tasks including trajectory generation, image inverse problems, and molecular design.

problem: Molecular property prediction requires effective integration of 2D graph structure and 3D conformer ensemble information, but existing methods use static geometric solvers or rigid fusion strategies.
approach: FACET employs a differentiable graph transformer that approximates Fused Gromov-Wasserstein for dynamic 2D-3D fusion and injects fragment-specific structural priors into attention layers.
contribution: FACET achieves state-of-the-art on molecular property, Boltzmann-weighted ensemble, and reaction-level prediction while providing 6x speedup and scaling to 75,000 molecules.
